subject: How to deal with very slow warm up due to large tree depth?

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: How to deal with very slow warm up due to large tree depth?
parts:
Hello,


I am trying to estimate a hierarchical negative binomial regression 

for multiply imputed data. Warm up is very slow (~75 samples after

72h, yes that’s hours!), which is partially due to the size of the data

(~190000 cases,  ~20 predictors, 22 groups) and the associated 

large number of parameters. 

However, I suspect that the main reason is the large tree depth value

 (around 14) during warm up, because if I run a non-hierarchical

model for the same data, that takes around the same time for the 

gradient evaluation, 150 warm up iterations plus 500 samples are 

done in 9h (tree depth during warm up is around 10 for this model). 


I think the large tree depth is partially due to me setting the target 

acceptance rate to .9, which I did because in earlier runs of a very

 similar model I found divergent iterations after warm up.


If I understood the section “58.2. HMC Algorithm Parameters” in the

stan reference correctly, one way reduce the tree depth is to increase

the step size, but I fear if I do this (via reducing the target acceptance

rate) I run the risk of getting divergent iterations again. Later under the

heading “” it reads:

“Poor behavior in the tails is the kind of pathology that can be uncovered

by running only a few warmup iterations. Looking at the acceptance 

probabilities and step sizes of the first few iterations provides an idea of

how bad the problem is and whether it must be addressed with modeling

efforts such as tighter priors or reparameterizations.”


I scaled all predictor variables and have used non-centered parameterization

where I know this is possible, but I am uncertain what problematic acceptance

probabilities and step size are. 


I am attaching diagnostic plots for a hierarchical and non-hierachical model,

the stan model for the hierarchical regression, and the output of the 

stan-summary for the non-hierachical model as further information. 

The parameters for sampling were 

num_samples=500 num_warmup=150 

algorithm=hmc engine=nuts max_depth=20 adapt delta=.90

init=0


I would be very thankful about any tips and/or pointers to where I do not

understand things correctly. 


Best - Guido



PS: The variational method results in rather implausible parameter values, even if I use the parameters I get with the optimizing approach as inits. But I must say that I know very little about how one maybe could improve the results of the variational method. It does not seem to work as a black box approach for my model/data.
